To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

work-related violence and alcohol abuse are associated with unprotected sex within regular partnerships among female sex workers, and that alcohol abuse may increase the risk associated with violence.
work-related violence was associated with unprotected sex between female sex workers (FSW) and their regular, paying partners.

1) violence against sex workers is associated both with inconsistent condom use with regular partners and with alcohol abuse among sex workers, 2) alcohol abuse may strengthen the effects of violence against sex workers on inconsistent condom use with partners and 3) interventions to reduce violence against sex workers may reduce HIV transmission.

the following questions.
understanding the relationship between violence, condom use and alcohol abuse among sex workers and their partners in Adama city, Ethiopia.
the relationship of work-related violence and inconsistent use of condoms among sex workers and their non-paying partners.

violence and alcohol use are associated with inconsistent condom with non-paying partners and these factors are more important than age, education, income, and the total number of sex partners in the past 7 days.
the findings of this study suggest that violence against establishment-based FSWs is associated with HIV risks within regular, nonpaying partnerships.
the violence and HIV risks are interlinked and that violence against female sex workers is a major public health issue.

sex workers in Ethiopia are at risk for HIV and other STIs from non-paying partners.
